title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.title: How you fall
chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

chapters.title: Your flirting style
chapters.teaser: What you think you're doing, what they think you're doing, and the one move that lands.

chapters.title: Your attachment pattern
chapters.teaser: Clingy, cool, steady or somewhere in between. How you hold on when you care.

chapters.title: Jealousy and your trigger
chapters.teaser: The exact thing that sets you off, and what you do instead of saying it.

chapters.teaser: Not your type. Your match. The kind of person and love that lets you relax.

text.how-you-fall: You fall like a sword is drawn: decisively and with commitment. Gyeong is raw metal, the axe, the blade that has to be forged. You don't do vague. You know pretty quickly if you're interested, and once you are, you pursue with clarity. No games, no hints, just "I like you, let's go to dinner." This directness is refreshing and a little intimidating. You fall for strength, honesty and people who don't fold the first time you push back. Respect comes first. Without it, attraction dies fast. When you love, you love loyally and protectively, the kind of partner who would fight the world for their person. The catch is that you can treat love a bit like a mission, and a mission sometimes forgets to stop and enjoy the view.
text.flirting: You flirt by challenging. You tease, debate, poke holes in their opinions and see if they push back. If they do, you're delighted. If they shrink, you lose interest. It's an unusual style, and with the right person it creates incredible sparks. With the wrong one it can feel like being cross-examined. You're also extremely honest, so compliments from you are rare and therefore powerful. When you say "you look good," people believe it. Your growth area is softness. Let yourself be playful without winning, or admit you're nervous. "I'm actually a bit nervous right now" from someone as confident as you is incredibly disarming. The blade is impressive. The hand that holds it gently is what people fall for.
text.attachment: Your pattern often looks avoidant, though it comes from independence, not fear. You're self-sufficient and value your freedom, so you don't like being needed in a clingy way and can feel suffocated if a partner wants constant check-ins. You also protect yourself by being strong. Vulnerability can feel like weakness, so you might keep softer feelings locked up, even from people you love. Underneath that armour, you're intensely loyal and deeply sentimental. You'd remember a promise for a decade. The work for you is letting someone see you uncertain, hurt or soft, and staying in the room while they see it. Strength isn't never needing anyone. Strength is choosing to need someone and trusting them with it.
text.jealousy: When you're jealous, you get sharp, fast. Your trigger is disloyalty or disrespect. If someone flirts with your partner, or your partner seems to enjoy it a little too much, you feel it as a breach of a code. Your first instinct might be to confront the situation directly, or to cut the person off, possibly both before breakfast. The intensity can scare people, even when you're technically right. The better move is pausing before the swing. Ask yourself what actually happened, then talk to your partner, not the rival. "That bothered me, can we talk about where the line is?" You're great at boundaries. Just make sure you set them in a conversation, not in a showdown.
text.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you love like a drill sergeant. You have standards, rules, and opinions on how your partner should handle their job, their friends and their sock drawer. You call it honesty. They sometimes call it criticism. Second flag: your pride. Apologizing feels like losing, so you'd rather go silent for two days than say "I was wrong." Third: all-or-nothing endings. When someone disappoints you badly enough, you can cut them out instantly and completely, no conversation, no closure. It feels clean. It also means you never find out whether it could have been fixed. You're a protector, and that's beautiful. Just remember your partner is not a recruit. They're the person you chose.
text.what-you-need: You need someone strong enough to stand next to you without being cut. A partner with their own spine, their own opinions and enough confidence to tell you no. You need respect in both directions, and honesty even when it's uncomfortable. You also need warmth, quietly. Someone who softens your edges without trying to blunt you, who brings fun and lightness into your very serious, very competent life. You do best with partners who give you independence and don't take your need for space personally. And you need someone patient enough to wait for your heart to open, because when it does, it's huge. The right person makes you feel like metal in a warm fire: shaped, not melted.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, you love like a sword. Loyal, protective, you'd fight the whole world for your person.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You'd also fight your person. About how they load the dishwasher.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just honest! Your compliments actually mean something.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Rare compliments, frequent corrections. Not a great ratio, babe.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Show them the soft side. Saying "I'm nervous" makes you more magnetic, not less.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: "I was wrong" won't kill you. Try it once and see.

spring.intro: Spring is Wood's season, and Metal controls Wood. A spring-born Gyeong Metal is an axe walking into a forest, surrounded by work to be done. In love you are action first: you pursue clearly, you protect fiercely, and you prove feelings through effort. The season gives you a lot to chase, which can make romance feel like a goal to achieve. You can win someone over and then lose interest in the maintenance, or treat their needs like tasks on a list. Earth, your resource, slows you down usefully: routine, patience, a partner who feels like home base. The bravest thing a warrior can do in love is stop working and simply stay.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Gyeong, you won them. Congratulations. Now the relationship starts, and it isn't a quest.

summer.intro: Summer is Fire's season, and Fire controls Metal. A summer-born Gyeong is iron in the forge: heated, pressured and, if it holds, tempered into something remarkable. In love you may have been drawn to intense, passionate people who test you. Arguments can feel like trials of strength, and you hate losing them. The forge gives you resilience and loyalty, but it can also make you brace for conflict even in calm relationships. Earth, which turns Fire's heat into support for Metal, is your answer: a partner who is steady rather than dramatic, and conversations that cool before they become verdicts. Strong does not have to mean unbreakable. You are allowed to soften.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Gyeong, you survived every fire. You don't need new ones to prove it.

autumn.intro: Autumn is Metal's own season, so an autumn-born Gyeong is the blade at its sharpest. You love with total loyalty and total honesty, often in the same blunt sentence. You know what you want, you say it, and you expect the same in return. That clarity is attractive and slightly intimidating. With doubled Metal, your blind spot is rigidity. You decide what a partner meant and stop listening, or you treat a small slip as a betrayal of principle. Fire refines Metal, and Water lets it flow. In love that means warmth and softness: a partner who melts your certainty a little, and a willingness to say 'tell me more' before 'that's wrong'.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Gyeong, you're right a lot. You're also lonely a lot. Those might be connected.

winter.intro: Winter is Water's season, and Metal produces Water. A winter-born Gyeong Metal is a blade cooling in a river: sharp but quietly drained by the cold current. You give a lot of yourself in love, often through advice, problem solving and protecting people from things they never knew happened. You may come across as emotionally cool when you are actually feeling a great deal and expressing none of it. Pouring yourself out without warmth leaves you rusty and withdrawn. Earth, your resource, and Fire, your refiner, both help: a reliable partner, a warm home, someone who tells you plainly that you matter. A blade that is cared for stays bright.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Gyeong, you protect everyone so quietly. Let one person know what it costs you.

strength.strong: A strong Gyeong Metal is a blade with too much edge. With plenty of Metal and Earth in your chart, you love with conviction, loyalty and very firm rules. You protect your partner fiercely and expect the same standard back. Your blind spot is overpowering through bluntness: winning arguments instead of resolving them, giving harsh feedback as proof of honesty, deciding the relationship's terms alone. Being right is not the same as being close. Try softening the delivery without changing the truth. Ask how they feel before telling them what you think. Strength is most attractive when it chooses gentleness.
strength.weak: A weak Gyeong Metal is a sword that has been through too many battles. With little Metal or Earth support, you still try to be the protector in love, but you are running on fumes. You hide vulnerability behind competence and keep fighting other people's battles while ignoring your own. Your blind spot is over-giving through duty. You stay loyal to partners who do not repay it, because leaving feels like breaking your word. Loyalty to yourself counts too. Choose people who sharpen you rather than dull you, and let someone defend you for a change.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood in your chart turns love into a growth plan. You want things to move forward, define the relationship, make progress, and slow phases make you restless. You can also be stubborn in arguments, holding your position like a tree in wind. In love this looks like big intentions and a little impatience. Balance it with Metal energy: clear agreements, pruning what isn't working, and accepting that some things are already finished growing. Not every relationship needs to become a forest. Some are perfect as a single, steady tree.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means beginnings are your hard part. You might wait for the other person to make the first move, define things, or suggest the next step, and you can stay in a comfortable but stuck situation for too long. Your love is real, it just doesn't push. Balance it by practising small starts: suggest the date, send the first text, say what you hope for out loud. Green things help as reminders, a plant by your bed, a green phone case. Love grows when someone plants it. Sometimes that someone is you.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your love bright, fast and a little combustible. You fall hard, flirt boldly and feel everything at full volume. The highs are glorious. The lows, when attention drops, feel like the lights went out. You can also lose interest once the excitement settles. Balance it with Water energy: slowing down, letting quiet evenings count, and sitting with feelings before reacting. Ask yourself if you love the person or the thrill. The best flame for you burns steady, not just bright.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means passion and visibility don't come easily in love. You might care deeply but struggle to show it, hold back affection until you're sure, or feel awkward with romantic gestures. People can mistake your reserve for disinterest. Balance it by letting warmth out in small, brave doses: a compliment, a hug that lasts a second longer, a little playfulness. Warm colours and sunlight help you feel more expressive. You don't need fireworks. You just need people to see that the light is on.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth makes you a steady, devoted partner who can get a little stuck. You value security, routine and loyalty, and you might stay in familiar patterns even when they've stopped making you happy. Change feels risky. You may also over-care, taking on your partner's problems as your own. Balance it with Wood energy: try something new together, plan an adventure, let the relationship grow in surprising directions. Safe is wonderful. Safe and alive is even better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means love can feel unsteady. You might worry about where things stand, struggle to settle into commitment, or jump between highs and lows. You can also find it hard to trust that someone will stay. Balance it by building small, reliable rituals: a weekly date, a regular call, a shared routine. Choose partners who are consistent rather than exciting. Earth tones and home-cooked meals help you feel grounded. Stability isn't boring. For you, it's what lets love feel safe enough to enjoy.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives you strong standards and very clear boundaries in love. You know what you want and what you won't tolerate, which is healthy, until it becomes rigid. You can be critical, quick to judge, or end things abruptly when disappointed. Balance it with Fire energy: warmth, forgiveness, play. Let small mistakes be small. Say the kind thing before the honest thing. Strong boundaries keep you safe. Soft edges let people actually come close enough to love you.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are your hard part in love. You might say yes when you mean no, stay too long, or let people treat you less well than you deserve because you don't want conflict. Your heart is open, sometimes too open. Balance it by practising clear, simple limits: "I'm not okay with that," without a long explanation. Decluttering and white or silver accents can help you feel sharper. Boundaries aren't walls. They're the frame that makes the picture of your love clear.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water makes your love deep, intuitive and sometimes overwhelming. You feel everything, read every mood and can get lost in emotional currents or imagined stories. You may also avoid commitment, drifting rather than choosing. Balance it with Earth energy: grounding conversations, practical plans, partners who are steady and clear. Write down what actually happened before reacting to what you feel happened. Your depth is beautiful. It just needs a shore so you don't get swept away.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means emotional depth and rest don't come easily in love. You might stay busy, keep conversations practical, or struggle to sit with vulnerable feelings, yours or your partner's. Love can feel like a to-do list. Balance it with slow, quiet moments: late talks, journaling, listening without fixing. Navy and black, water by your bed, and slow evenings help you soften. You don't need to drown in feelings. Just let yourself wade in a little deeper.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you want it defined, labelled and growing by Thursday. Breathe.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your hope is beautiful. Let it grow at the speed of a real person.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: you fall hard, fast and loudly. Then the second act bores you.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is a gift. Let it simmer a while. Slow love tastes better.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: staying somewhere stale because leaving takes effort isn't loyalty. It's inertia.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Make sure it's going somewhere that still feeds you.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: your dating checklist has forty points. Nobody passes. Including you.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Standards protect you. Leave one door open for someone surprising.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: you wrote a whole love story in your head. They've read none of it.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is gorgeous. Share a little of it with the real person.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Love won't start itself. Send the first text. Plant something.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Waiting for them to make the move isn't patience. It's hiding behind a nice word.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? Your love is real, it just whispers. Let someone hear it.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: A compliment you only think doesn't count. Say it, then survive the blushing.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? You love brightly but drift. A small weekly ritual keeps you anchored.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Three crushes, zero follow-through. Pick one and show up twice in a row.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? Your kindness needs a boundary. A no keeps your yes worth something.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Three cancellations and a fourth chance isn't generosity. It's a pattern you're funding.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? You act before you feel. Pause and ask what you actually want.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Over someone in a weekend isn't healing. It's skipping the chapter. Read it.
